claims: A fuse contains a thin wire that melts when excessive electric current passes through it.
When the wire melts, it breaks the circuit and stops the flow of electricity.
This protects household appliances from damage caused by power surges or short circuits.

claims.text: A fuse is an automatic means of removing power from a faulty system by melting when excess current or a short circuit occurs.
The speed at which a fuse blows depends on the amount of current flowing through it and the material it is made of.
